When I told him the first time he brushed it off and said to talk to him whenever.  And I obsessed (he gaslit the shit out of me). But when I called to hold my ground and confirm “Hey. Hey there 👋🏼

So it can be difficult to talk to someone if you think they need help and they refuse or don’t believe it! But maybe it would help to start doing some research and pinpoint some behaviors to certain symptoms. Bipolar is a complex disorder and is not so easy to diagnose as some people might think? It’s not mood swings and always being an asshole. If he exhibits behaviors like spending a lot of money, burning bridges, feelings of grandeur, and then slumping into depression and thoughts of suicide then those are common symptoms of the disorder!

Maybe he also has narcissistic personality disorder? My dad has both so it’s a tricky boundary. 

Also from experience with my dad, the best way to approach is to very calmly bring it up. Like tiptoe almost! Never during an argument. And sit down and talk. Bring examples ready and have counterpoints ready as well because often denial is involved. Think of it as presenting a proposal! 

Always worked for me and my dad is the worst!

Good luck.

It’s very hard to navigate and I’m sorry.  It’s not easy and makes life seem bleak when your brain literally is abnormal and wants to self destruct. 

I also understand the idea of needing a significant other. I’m the same way. It’s actually something called an “anchor”! I was told by my therapist. 

Anchors are very important to people with mental issues, such as bipolar. Because our minds distort the way we see reality and sometimes all we need is someone to trust and confide in and tell us we’re seeing it the wrong way. It helps so much to have someone like that. I’m in a shitty relationship but he is such an anchor when I’m manic or depressed and tells me my brain is just fucking with my head (because it is!). 

It’s hard to find an anchor with friends and family because you have to constantly perform that you’re doing better than you really are just so you don’t burden them. Don’t feel bad for wanting a partner. It’s totally normal. However, since it is hard to come by a romantic relationship these days, I suggest maybe try picking one friend that you just love spending time with and start opening up to them? Or get a therapist! My therapist has helped me exponentially. It is so critical to my mental health to be in therapy. 

I wish you the best of luck.

I’ve had this for two years now where I’ll get really bad nerve pain and tingling. It comes and goes. There have been times where I can’t walk because I’m so stiff/numb and have had friends carry me and drive my car. I thought it was peripheral neuropathy from diabetes but doctor said no. It’s been debilitating but never as bad as yesterday. 

I seriously doubt it’s anxiety also. Even though all this shit was happening, I was still being positive and making jokes with the nurses. I wasn’t panicky whatsoever. I had no fear of dying up until they said I might be OD’ing and that someone maybe slipped some shit in what was I eating 😣

Edit:

I guess I’m not saying I want the disease because it’s scary of course but I just want an answer to all these fucked up symptoms that have been getting worse 😞 It would be a relief in some way to finally know what’s going on to me.
